newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rates stable, demand on rise.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rates stable, demand on rise.

text.p: Croatian interbank rates were stable on Monday amid growing cash demands and with many banks reporting shortages, dealers said.
"It was no simple task to find money for all the banks in need but trade was good, all things considered," dealer Jasenka Blagajic said.
A total of 40.1 million kuna were settled by 1100 local (0900 GMT), leaving only a three million kuna shortage. Some lenders withdrew 20 million kuna in earlier placements.
Call money, at a stable 10.5 percent rate, accounted for 90 percent of fresh borrowings by 16 banks.
One-month loans were granted at 16 percent.
Overnight trade totalled 43.3 million over the weekend as seven banks sought funds to replenish thin accounts. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
